newsitem.title: SPAIN: Ex-Madrid air cargo rates to up 5-10pct as busines.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Madrid air cargo rates to up 5-10pct as busines.

text.p: Many airlines flying from Spain are preparing to raise their cargo rates by between five and 10 percent from the end of this month and some have done so already, airline officials and freight forwarders said.
This is the first major price increase, excluding last November's fuel surcharge, in two years, they said.

Current prices, quoted above, are already higher than January's for transatlantic routes although only 25 percent of forwarders and carriers surveyed have increased their quoted rates so far. Most of the others said they would do so from late March or the beginning of April.
Rises will affect most routes, with the exception in some cases of the North Atlantic.
"Some airlines have put up rates already and I expect the rest to do so any day now," said a freight forwarder with substantial transatlantic business.

"We are in the process of raising prices. It depends on the destination but the increase will be approximately seven percent from Spain," said Carlos Medina, cargo sales manager for Lufthansa. The increase will apply from April 1, he added.
British Airways is preparing to raise prices from March 26 on some routes from Spain and is still finalising details of which routes and by how much.
"Some will go up, others won't, but none will come down," said BA's cargo manager Vicente Das.

The price increase will coincide with a temporary reduction in BA's cargo capacity from Spain. It is replacing the twice daily Boeing 767 service to London with narrowbody 757s, implying a loss of 10 to 12 tonnes a day of cargo capacity between Spain and London. The widebodies will return on May 10 when passenger and freight business picks up for the summer season.
One of the major U.S. airlines flying from Spain said it would not increase its rates while another said it would, by between five and 10 percent.

"We'll stick with the same rates because the North Atlantic is very competitive. People are paying the same rates to New York as to Copenhagen for example," said an official at one of the big U.S. airlines.
Iberia has already raised rates for new business to Latin America and will put up its prices across the board over the next few weeks with increases of around 10 percent.
"The idea was to have put up general prices this month, but there have been delays for other reasons," a cargo official at the Spanish airline said.

It is more difficult to raise prices on North Atlantic routes, simply because there are so flights from Europe that cargo rates tend to be low, but more than half the airlines , GSAs and forwarders surveyed said they were planning to do so.
Malaysian Airlines Systems Bhd Ltd is raising its rates to Asia but Air Europa and CSA Czech Airlines are not increasing their prices, according to the general sales agent who handles all three.
Rate rises apart, business this month is booming, airlines said.

The peak season for fresh fruit and vegetable exports lasts until early April and manufactured goods exports are also buoyant, helped by steady economic growth in Spain and the peseta's fall against the dollar this year.

Figures released this week showed that economic growth picked up to 2.6 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of last year compared with 2.2 percent in the third quarter. Exports grew by 12.1 percent.
Exports will have been boosted still further this year. Since January 1 the dollar has risen to 143 pesetas from 129.
"The lower peseta is having a positive effect on exports," Lufthansa's Medina said.
"There's too much cargo for us to handle," said an official at a U.S. airline. "It should ease from April."
Airlines reported good demand for space for car components, shoes and manufactured goods. As in previous months, exports of telecommunications equipment to Latin America are particularly strong.
Tomatoes are dominating bulk exports of perishable products to New York, but this will fall in April when the Dutch tomato season starts, airline officials said.
